title: Meaning of 'string band' versus brass band
summary: String band meant a full dance orchestra with horns and drums, while brass band meant the street band; the term faded out.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: A snare drum. It was a good snare drum. You mentioned like a string band now. Does that mean with the trumpet and trombone and all too? Yeah.
We used to call it string band because they'd have the guitar and the bass.
But it didn't mean just the guitar and bass and mandolin or violin or something. It meant the full dance band. Uh-huh.
And we would call the brass band, you know, the nine pieces or the twelve pieces like that on the streets. Yeah.
That was the brass band. Yeah. And the string band meant a regular dance orchestra. That's right.
How far back did they use that term, string band?
Oh, they used it during my time. I heard it, you know, string band. But they didn't use it awfully, too often.
They don't use that now anymore. No, they don't use that anymore. Like they wouldn't call Sweet Emmas a string band. I know. First they had string bass but no guitars. Uh-huh.
But they died out. You know, people never used it too much. I heard the elder people used it.
That's what I know it was used a long time ago. Now I'm sort of surprised when I hear people talking about a string band.

Because years ago I thought they meant like a string trio. Yeah, I know what you mean. With guitar, bass, mandolin, or violins, yeah. Something without any horns. Right. But the string band meant with the horns and all then, too. And drums and all, too, in the string band. Yeah.
Yeah, it's interesting that they used that term. Uh-huh. Any other favorite drummers that you had that you can think of that were good in those days?
